essence: The chapter presents a fuller, guna-specific restatement of prior supreme knowledge, yielding siddhi and certainty.
Reliance on this knowledge and attainment of sameness with the speaker frees one from birth in creation and distress in dissolution.
Creation is the Lord's self-power sowing seed in the Brahman-womb; knowing this cause makes release easy.
Brahman, as great womb, and the speaker, as seed-giver and father, are the primordial source and nourishing power of all forms.
Nature's three qualities bind the imperishable self by making it identify with guna-dharmas for enjoyment and liberation.
